lead: Hi, I’m Gromit. I don’t say much. I design things that make people read twice.

blocks.body:
I grew up in a busy family. My father works long hours at a job he can’t really talk about. My mother works at City Hall and is much stronger than she looks. My little sister always seems to know what I’m thinking. Somebody had to keep the house running, so I learned early to notice what was going wrong and quietly fix it.

I also learned to say things without words. A raised eyebrow, a sign on the fridge, a drawing left on the kitchen table. Graphic design was the obvious next step. Most of my work starts with a sentence and ends as a poster, a book or a film.

blocks.heading: How I work
blocks.body: I like the moment a viewer realizes the form is saying something the words alone can’t. A circle of greetings that becomes a calendar. A book you can’t read in order. I care just as much about showing how I got there, so every project on this site includes the process along with the result.

blocks.heading: What I’m looking for
blocks.body: A junior role on a team that cares about ideas, where I can learn from senior designers and bring my own voice to the work. Editorial, cultural and brand projects interest me most. I graduate in June 2027 and I’m happy to relocate to New York or Chicago.

blocks.heading: Outside the studio
blocks.body: I bake bread most mornings, a habit from summers at a bakery in Wigan. I build model railways, sometimes at speed. I run a lettering club where the cheese is as important as the type. And I walk Bond, our family dog, who always seems to know where we’re going before I do.
